script: The computer that landed Apollo 11 on the Moon had about 4 kilobytes of working memory. Apollo 11 touched down on the Moon on July 20, 1969. The guidance computer weighed about 32 kilograms. Its programs were stored in rope memory, with wires woven through tiny magnetic rings by hand. During the landing, alarms flashed because the computer was overloaded. It kept working by dropping less important tasks, and the landing went ahead. Follow WonderBytes for more facts that sound fake but are true.
